title: Experiment: the `app/server/` adapter door, verified in both directions
summary: Two adapters were built over `lib/` — `content.js` and `stages.js` — each beginning with `import "server-only"` and re-exporting by explicit name. A Server Component importing both compiled, appeared in the route table as `○ /probe-adapters`, served HTTP 200, and reported every imported binding resolved to a real value (`function,object,function,function`). A `'use client'` module importing one of them FAILED the build at `./app/server/content.js:1:1`, quoting the offending source line with a caret and printing the import chain from the page through the client module to the adapter; `next build` exited 1 with the violation present and 0 once it was removed. Both probe routes were deleted afterwards and the tree rebuilt clean.

facts.layout: app/ at the repository root, adapters at app/server/

omissions.reason: Turbopack is the default at 16.3.2 and was the only builder exercised. AST-0032 measured the UNGUARDED failure mode as a Turbopack internal error, and whether webpack reports it differently was not tested here either.

The client violation imported an adapter directly. A chain that reaches `lib/` through an intermediate module was not exercised — that is the bypass path TSK-0006's static check is required to detect, and it is not this task's.

notes: ⚠️ THE ROUTE TABLE CAUGHT A SILENT FAILURE AGAIN, on the second consecutive task. The probe was first placed at `app/_probe/`, the build succeeded, and the route never appeared: a leading underscore marks a PRIVATE FOLDER in the App Router and opts the directory out of routing. `✓ Compiled successfully` was printed either way. TSK-0003 hit the same class through `src/app/` precedence; the shape is 'a build that succeeds while rendering nothing you wrote', and only the route table distinguishes them. ⚠️ The wording of the client-side diagnostic is deliberately NOT recorded as a required string. ACC-0027 forbids asserting it, because Next.js produced two different messages for this violation reached two ways and one of them named the wrong router.
